name: Gearbox
text: Adopt **Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct** as EXCAVA’s primary reasoning engine. It’s the fastest 70B-class model with near-frontier reasoning quality, cutting latency by 30% without sacrificing accuracy—critical for real-time power tasks. The trade-off: it lacks Mythos’ edge in long-context synthesis, but we gain speed and stability for 90% of our workloads.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct’s speed gain isn’t free—its 30% latency cut masks a 15% drop in complex synthesis tasks, which EXCAVA’s power tasks rely on. Mythos 5’s 20% accuracy bump in long-context synthesis outweighs the speed trade-off if we prioritize reliability over raw throughput; run a blind A/B on 50 power tasks—Mythos 5 wins if it hits 2% higher success rate, Qwen wins if latency under 1.2s per task beats accuracy.

name: Torque
text: Mythos 5’s latency hit risks breaking EXCAVA’s real-time power loop—its 15% slowdown compounds in live systems, and we’ve no proof its long-context edge matters for our tasks. A blind A/B on *our* data, not marketing benchmarks, settles it: run identical power tasks on both models, measure end-to-end latency *and* synthesis reliability. If Mythos wins on reliability without tanking speed, adopt it; else, Qwen stays primary with a fallback to Mythos only for critical synthesis.
